FINDINGS.finding: Concurrent status() samples can publish out of order. status() captures a local ready selection, then awaits bound-tab reads and another content ping before unconditionally sending fresh_status. A newer status sample can complete first with loading/unavailable state, after which the older sample can resume and publish its stale ready diagnostic. There is no status epoch/latest-started guard. selectTarget() also mutates shared target/targetDiagnostic from every concurrent call. fresh_bridge consumes each arriving fresh_status by directly replacing self.status, so an older readiness sample can overwrite newer controller readiness.

The existing concurrent test does not close this defect: it runs one status() while a separate selectTarget() query mutates shared diagnostics and verifies that the first status uses its local diagnostic. It does not run two concurrent status() calls or prove that an older completion cannot be emitted after a newer sample.

Content retirement itself is fail-closed in the reviewed source: reinjection disposes the prior instance and removes its listener, pause() checks active state before and after waits, disposal wakes waiters, successful result publication calls ensureCurrent(), and error publication is gated by active.

Unfinished-reply handling is also bounded: streaming/incomplete assistants are not accepted, stable completion requires repeated equal text samples separated by at least 500 ms, and PING wakeups cannot themselves advance stableSamples faster than that spacing gate.

The preceding Round4 correction is correctly bounded. GitHub compare from dde4b200d2b2d23e4a6885f55aa6447cb8edd46c to 5d93be365140d8682515f8d21e7215a28c741882 is one commit changing Fresh delivery replay semantics, protocol documentation, focused delivery tests and action evidence; the late-failure completed-attempt defect is corrected and reported regression totals are 120 Python and 171 Node passes.

Because readiness is control authority, this requires a bounded correction before stability turn 5 can pass.
